vercel.label: Vercel
vercel.comment: Some skills declare a name that differs from their directory. Skills are addressed by declared name on install and by directory upstream, so the ones that differ are mapped here. A new mismatch shows up in `audit` as an undeclared skill.

web.description: React, Next.js, Tailwind. The mje.fi profile.

cli.description: Command-line tools and services with no UI surface. The exy profile.

global.description: Installed once at user level, not per project.

vercel/deploy-to-vercel.reason: Instructs the agent to run `git commit` and `git push`. Policy beats precedence: the diff-only rule outranks the tier order.
vercel/deploy-to-vercel.recheck: If upstream gains a no-push mode, reconsider.

vercel/vercel-cli-with-tokens.reason: Same — documents `git commit` and `git push` as the preferred deploy path.
vercel/vercel-cli-with-tokens.recheck: If upstream gains a no-push mode, reconsider.

jakub/better-accessibility.reason: Competes with vercel/web-design-guidelines on "check accessibility". Tier 2 beats tier 3.
jakub/better-accessibility.recheck: Jakub's version is deeper (6 reference files). Swap if WIG coverage proves too shallow.

jakub/better-writing.reason: Competes with vercel/writing-guidelines on "review my copy". Tier 2 beats tier 3.

jakub/better-interface.reason: Auto-triggering aggregator over the better-* set. Fires on any "review my UI", colliding with web-design-guidelines, then re-enters the individual skills.
jakub/better-interface.note: interface-review is the same review, explicit-invoke only, so it never competes for a trigger.

jakub/teardown.reason: Technical illustration of physical objects, not interface work, and no project in the set draws them. Auto-triggers, and ships its own render and test scripts.
jakub/teardown.recheck: Include the day a project needs technical illustrations.

emil/emil-design-eng.reason: Auto-triggering umbrella over Emil's own set. Overlaps animate, review-animations and better-ui without adding a distinct job.

emil/break-ui.reason: Same job as jakub/break — worst-case data on a throwaway page — but auto-triggers on "stress-test" and "find edge cases", taking the request from the explicit-invoke break. Static interface is Jakub's domain.
emil/break-ui.recheck: If break's scenarios miss values that break-ui's CATALOG.md covers, swap.

emil/ask-sonner.reason: Sonner is not in the stack.
emil/ask-sonner.recheck: Include the day a project adds the sonner dependency.

routing.rule: Emil's skills own motion. jakub/better-ui is installed for static polish only — surfaces, icons, concentric radius, optical alignment, hit areas. Ignore its animations.md, enter-exit.md and icon-transitions.md.
mine/improve is explicit-invoke only and covers the whole repo. emil/improve-animations auto-triggers and covers motion alone. They share an output shape, not a scope.

karpathy/karpathy-guidelines governs how a change is made: assumptions, size, what it may touch, how it is verified. vercel/react-best-practices fires on the same "writing, reviewing, or refactoring" trigger and governs React and Next patterns. They share a trigger, not a job. Where the guidelines say stop and ask, Long runs still holds: ask before the first edit, and mid-run stop only for a question the code cannot answer.
